fields.subnational_unit: Ontario, Canada (First Nation and non-First Nation communities)
fields.population: 143 First Nation drinking-water systems (137 communities) with federal risk evaluations, and 55 responding municipal and township systems (survey; 54 usable)
fields.sample_size: 143 First Nation systems (INAC risk evaluation surveys) and 54 municipalities/townships completing the same risk-evaluation survey (9 serving under 500 people, 26 serving 500-5,000, 20 serving over 5,000)
fields.effect_measure: federal Risk Level Evaluation Guidelines scores (source, design, operation, reporting, operator; weighted 10/30/30/10/20) summarised as low/medium/high risk per system; descriptive comparison of First Nation vs municipal systems
fields.effect_estimate: Overall risk (Tables 6-7): First Nation systems 55 low, 62 medium, 26 high (of 143); municipal systems 54 low, 0 medium, 0 high (of 54). By category (high risk): source water 72 vs 4, design 49 vs 0, operation 32 vs 2, reporting 30 vs 0, operator 12 vs 0. Only 27 First Nations reported a source water protection plan versus 50 municipalities. The text elsewhere says 49 of 143 systems were ranked high risk and 63 exceeded federal health parameters (inconsistent with the 26 in Table 6; no data for 30 systems). Authors argue provincial regulation, funding and technical capacity explain the gap and that the federal government has a constitutional responsibility to ensure equivalent standards.
fields.model_type: descriptive comparison of categorical risk rankings (counts)
fields.study_design: cross-sectional descriptive comparison of administrative risk evaluations (First Nation) with a purpose-run municipal survey
fields.section: Full text (International Indigenous Policy Journal 3(3):8): Introduction; Methods and data; Results (Tables 3-7); Conclusion
fields.exact_location: Risk evaluation system p5-9 (Tables 3-5); data p10-11; Tables 6-7 p12; Conclusion p22

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a descriptive comparison of federal drinking-water risk evaluations for 143 First Nation systems and 54 municipal systems in Ontario, read in full text 2026-10-04. No municipal system scored above low risk, whereas 26 of 143 First Nation systems were high risk and 62 medium (Table 6); source-water protection plans reported by 27 First Nations versus 50 municipalities. Descriptive, non-causal; the paper's own text and table disagree on the number of high-risk First Nation systems (49 vs 26).
pdf_note: International Indigenous Policy Journal 3(3):8 (2012), 26 pp; about 58,700 characters read; figures not read
notes: Abstract-level extraction was vague ('greater health risks'); full text gives counts. EFFECT-SIZE CANDIDATE (Family: administrative/regulatory capacity gap, counts per risk class) -- not added (A13). Internal inconsistency: 49 vs 26 high-risk First Nation systems.
